newsitem.title: GREECE: Drachma resilient vs mark - Citibank.
newsitem.headline: Drachma resilient vs mark - Citibank.

text.p: The drachma will be resilient versus the mark, spending most of its time in the 155/160 band in the short-term and enjoying plenty of interest rate protection that leaves room for lower rates, Citibank London said in its February report.
Market sentiment about economic prospects remained positive but better inflation figures were key to further interest rate cuts, Citibank said.
However short-term interest rate projections of 7.9 percent at end-1997 in Greece's convergence plan looked overly optimistic with the independence of the Bank of Greece planned for 1997, it said.
Bank of Greece is scheduled to gain independence before the end of 1997.
Inflation is expected to average 7.0 percent in 1997, overshooting the official 6.5 percent target from 8.5 percent in 1996, Citibank said.
The report was written before the central bank slashed its overnight intervention bid by 50 basis points to 11.90 percent last Friday.
Greece's revised CPI inflation fell to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January from 7.3 percent in December.

"So far, the Bank of Greece has been very succesful in managing the drachma," it said while acknowledging that a strong currency strategy was necessary to bring Greece closer to EU norms despite a widening current account deficit. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
